w: -2⁴ means -(2 × 2 × 2 × 2) = -16, which is negative. The exponent applies only to 2, not to the negative sign.

n.0: -3 × (-5) = 15; two negatives multiply to a positive.
n.1: (-1)⁵ = -1, and -1 × (-6) = 6, which is positive.
n.3: (-2)⁴ = 16; the parentheses include the sign, and four negative factors give a positive.

q: A lab report states that a urine culture contains 3.2 × 10⁵ bacteria per milliliter. How is this number written in standard form?
w: A positive exponent of 5 moves the decimal point 5 places right: 3.2 → 320,000.

n.0: 0.000032 moves the decimal point left, which is what a negative exponent does.
n.2: 3,200,000 moves the decimal point 6 places; the exponent is 5.
n.3: 32,000 moves the decimal point only 4 places.

q: The diameter of a human red blood cell is about 0.0000075 meter. How is this length written in scientific notation?
w: Move the decimal point right until one nonzero digit is in front of it: 0.0000075 → 7.5 takes 6 moves. Moving right for a small number gives a negative exponent: 7.5 × 10⁻⁶.

n.0: 7.5 × 10⁻⁷ = 0.00000075, which has one zero too many; reaching 7.5 from 0.0000075 takes 6 moves, not 7.
n.1: A positive exponent gives a large number (7,500,000); a number less than 1 needs a negative exponent.
n.2: This counts only 5 moves; 7.5 × 10⁻⁵ = 0.000075.

q: In a review of exponent rules, a student is asked to simplify 2³ × 2⁴ ÷ 2⁵. What is the value of the expression?
w: Same base: add exponents when multiplying and subtract when dividing: 2^(3 + 4 - 5) = 2² = 4.

n.0: 128 = 2⁷ comes from multiplying the first two exponents (3 × 4 = 12) and then subtracting 5.
n.2: 4,096 = 2¹² adds all three exponents; dividing by 2⁵ means subtracting 5.
n.3: 2 is the exponent, not the value; 2² = 4.

q: A square patio has an area of 90 square feet, so each side is √90 feet long. Between which two consecutive whole numbers does √90 lie?
w: 9² = 81 and 10² = 100. Since 81 < 90 < 100, √90 is between 9 and 10 (about 9.49).

n.0: 45 is 90 ÷ 2; taking a square root is not the same as halving the number.
n.1: 9² = 81, which is already less than 90, so √90 is greater than 9.
n.3: 10² = 100, which is already greater than 90, so √90 is less than 10.

q: A student in a prerequisite math course evaluates the expression 5² + 3 × 2³ - √64 by hand. What is the value of the expression? Enter the number only.
w: Exponents and roots first: 5² = 25, 2³ = 8 and √64 = 8. Multiply: 3 × 8 = 24. Then add and subtract left to right: 25 + 24 - 8 = 41.

q: A large hospital system processes about 6 × 10⁸ lab results per year, and a small clinic processes about 3 × 10⁵. How many times as many results does the hospital system process as the clinic? Enter the number only.

tr.3: Subtracted the coefficients (6 - 3) instead of dividing and ignored the powers of 10.

q: A tutor writes several expressions on the board and asks which are equal to 1/16. Which of the following expressions are equal to 1/16? Select all that apply.
w: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: 2⁻⁴ = 1/2⁴ = 1/16 and 4⁻² = 1/4² = 1/16. Also (1/2)⁴ = 1/16.

n.1: (1/4)⁻² flips the fraction: 4² = 16, not 1/16.
n.2: Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1, so 16⁰ = 1.
n.5: -2⁴ = -16; the negative sign is not an exponent and it does not make a reciprocal.

q: In a review of the power-of-a-power rule, a student is asked to find the value of (3²)³. What is the value of the expression?
w: Power of a power: multiply the exponents. (3²)³ = 3⁶ = 729. Check: 3² = 9 and 9³ = 729.

n.0: 27 multiplies 9 by 3 instead of cubing 9.
n.2: 6,561 = 3⁸ uses 2³ = 8 as the exponent instead of 2 × 3 = 6.
n.3: 243 = 3⁵ adds the exponents (2 + 3); for a power of a power, multiply them.

q: A microscopic cell is 2 × 10⁻³ centimeter long. A researcher models 6 × 10⁴ of these cells lined up end to end. What is the total length?
w: Multiply the coefficients and add the exponents: (2 × 6) × 10^(-3 + 4) = 12 × 10¹ = 120 cm.

n.1: 1,200 cm uses 10² after writing 12; 12 × 10¹ is 120.
n.2: 12 cm rewrites 12 × 10¹ as 1.2 × 10¹ without raising the exponent; 12 × 10¹ = 1.2 × 10² = 120.
n.3: 80 cm adds the coefficients (2 + 6) instead of multiplying them.

q: A student in a placement test review must find the value of 5⁰ + 5⁻¹ + 5¹. What is the value of the expression?

n.0: 1 treats 5⁻¹ as -5 (1 - 5 + 5); a negative exponent gives a reciprocal, not a negative number.
n.1: 0 treats 5⁰ as 0 and 5⁻¹ as -5.
n.2: 5.2 treats 5⁰ as 0; any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1.

q: A square floor tile in a hospital lobby has an area of 0.81 square meter. What is the length of one side of the tile?
w: Side = √0.81. Because 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, the side is 0.9 m.

n.0: 0.405 is 0.81 ÷ 2; a square root is not half the number.
n.3: 0.2025 is 0.81 ÷ 4, which treats the area like a perimeter.

q: A science student must simplify (8 × 10⁵) ÷ (2 × 10⁻²) and give the result in scientific notation. Which is the result?
w: Divide the coefficients: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Subtract the exponents: 5 - (-2) = 7. Result: 4 × 10⁷.

n.0: 4 × 10⁻¹⁰ multiplies the exponents (5 × -2).
n.2: 1.6 × 10⁴ multiplies the coefficients (8 × 2 = 16) while adding the exponents.
n.3: 4 × 10³ computes 5 + (-2) = 3; dividing powers of 10 means subtracting, and 5 - (-2) = 7.

q: Four students each completed part of the same online module. The parts completed were 5/9, 4/7, 6/11 and 7/13. Which fraction of the module is greatest?
w: Convert to decimals: 4/7 ≈ 0.571, 5/9 ≈ 0.556, 6/11 ≈ 0.545, 7/13 ≈ 0.538. The greatest is 4/7. (Cross-multiplying 4/7 and 5/9 also works: 4 × 9 = 36 > 5 × 7 = 35.)

n.0: 5/9 ≈ 0.556, slightly less than 4/7 ≈ 0.571 (cross products 35 < 36).
n.1: 7/13 ≈ 0.538 is actually the least; a larger denominator does not mean a larger fraction.
n.2: 6/11 ≈ 0.545; its larger numerator and denominator do not make it larger.

q: A pharmacy compares the active-ingredient fractions of five generic products. Place the values in order from least to greatest, starting with the least: 0.4, 38%, 7/20, 0.305, 3/8.
w: Convert each value to a decimal: 0.305; 7/20 = 0.35; 3/8 = 0.375; 38% = 0.38; 0.4 = 0.400. Least to greatest: 0.305 < 0.35 < 0.375 < 0.38 < 0.4. Adding zeros to compare (0.380 vs 0.375 vs 0.400) avoids the trap of thinking more digits means a bigger number.

q: A nursing student must choose the list that is written in order from least to greatest. Which list is in order from least to greatest?
w: As decimals: -1/2 = -0.5, -0.4, 0.04 and 1/5 = 0.2. The number farther left of 0 is smaller, so -0.5 < -0.4 < 0.04 < 0.2.

n.0: 1/5 = 0.2 is greater than 0.04, so it must come last.
n.2: -0.4 is greater than -0.5 because it is closer to 0; this list orders the negatives by absolute value.
n.3: Both negative numbers are less than 0.04, so they must come first.

q: A dietitian compares the fraction of daily sodium in four meals: 45%, 0.5, 4/9 and 0.449. Which value is the least?
w: Convert each to a decimal: 45% = 0.450, 0.5 = 0.500, 4/9 = 0.444... and 0.449. Comparing digit by digit, 0.444... is the least, so 4/9 is the least.

n.0: 0.449 is greater than 4/9 = 0.444... (compare the thousandths: 9 > 4).
n.1: 0.5 is the greatest of the four values.
n.2: 45% = 0.45, which is greater than both 0.449 and 0.444...

q: On a math placement test, a student must decide which inequality statement is true. Which statement is true?
w: 5/12 = 0.41666..., which is less than 0.42 (0.416... < 0.420), so the statement is true.

q: Overnight low temperatures, in degrees Celsius, were recorded at five weather stations: -2/3, -0.6, -3/4, -5/8 and -0.7. Place the temperatures in order from least to greatest, starting with the least.
w: As decimals: -3/4 = -0.75, -0.7, -2/3 ≈ -0.667, -5/8 = -0.625, -0.6. For negative numbers, the one farther from 0 is smaller, so least to greatest is -0.75 < -0.7 < -0.667 < -0.625 < -0.6.

q: Four patients' meal trays were checked after lunch. Ana ate 5/8 of her meal, Ben ate 0.63 of his, Carmen ate 61% of hers and Dev ate 3/5 of his. Who ate the greatest portion?
w: Convert to decimals: Ana 5/8 = 0.625, Ben 0.63 = 0.630, Carmen 61% = 0.61, Dev 3/5 = 0.6. The greatest is 0.630, so Ben ate the most.

n.0: 5/8 = 0.625, which is slightly less than 0.630.
n.1: 61% = 0.61, which is less than 0.625 and 0.63.
n.2: 3/5 = 0.6, the least of the four portions.

q: A pharmacy technician needs a value that is greater than 1/3 but less than 3/8. Which value lies between 1/3 and 3/8?
w: 1/3 = 0.333... and 3/8 = 0.375. 0.35 is greater than 0.333... and less than 0.375, so it lies between them.

n.0: 0.38 is greater than 3/8 = 0.375, so it is above the range.
n.2: 0.33 is less than 1/3 = 0.333..., so it is below the range.
n.3: 2/5 = 0.4, which is greater than 3/8.

q: Four lab measurements are recorded as 1.105, 1 1/8, 1.09 and 112%. Place the measurements in order from greatest to least, starting with the greatest.
Four race times, in minutes, are listed in different forms. Which list shows the times in descending order (greatest to least)?

n.0: 2.205 is less than 2 1/4 = 2.250, so it must come after 2 1/4.
n.1: This list is in ascending order (least to greatest), the reverse of what is asked.
n.3: 2.205 is not the greatest; having more digits does not make a decimal larger (2.205 < 2.3).

q: A clinic's goal is for each team to complete more than 0.7 of its training modules. Which of the following completion values are greater than 0.7? Select all that apply.

n.2: 9/13 ≈ 0.692, which is less than 0.7.

q: Four bank accounts end the month with small negative balances, in thousands of dollars: -0.25, -0.215, -0.31 and -0.205. Which balance is the greatest?
w: For negative numbers, the one closest to 0 is greatest. Compare absolute values: 0.205 < 0.215 < 0.25 < 0.31, so -0.205 is the greatest.

n.0: -0.215 is farther from 0 than -0.205 (0.215 > 0.205), so it is smaller.
n.2: -0.25 is farther from 0 than -0.205, so it is smaller.
n.3: -0.31 is the least of the four; a larger absolute value means a smaller negative number.

q: On a horizontal number line, point P is plotted at -2.6. Between which two consecutive integers is point P located?
w: -2.6 is less than -2 and greater than -3 (-3 < -2.6 < -2), so P lies between -3 and -2, a little closer to -3.

n.0: -2.6 is greater than -3, so it lies to the right of -3.
n.2: This ignores the negative sign; 2.6 lies between 2 and 3.
n.3: -2.6 is less than -2, so it lies to the left of -2, not between -2 and -1.

q: A number line runs from 0 to 2, with tick marks every 1/4 unit starting at 0. Point A is on the 7th tick mark to the right of 0. What is the value of point A?
w: Each tick is 1/4 unit, so 7 ticks to the right of 0 is 7 × 1/4 = 7/4 = 1 3/4.

n.0: 7/8 treats each tick as 1/8, as if the 8 intervals covered 0 to 1 instead of 0 to 2.
n.1: 1 1/2 = 6/4 counts the tick at 0 as the first tick mark.
n.3: 1.7 treats each tick as 0.1; the ticks are quarters, not tenths.

q: In a review of absolute value, a student evaluates the expression |-8| - |3 - 11|. What is the value of the expression?
w: Work inside the absolute value bars first: 3 - 11 = -8, and |-8| = 8. The first term is |-8| = 8. So 8 - 8 = 0.

n.0: -6 drops the bars and subtracts both 3 and 11 (8 - 3 - 11); the bars group 3 - 11, so find -8 first and then |-8| = 8.
n.2: -16 treats |-8| as -8 and then subtracts 8.
n.3: 16 leaves |3 - 11| as -8, then subtracts: 8 - (-8). An absolute value cannot be negative.

q: On a number line used to track a patient's weight change in pounds from a baseline, point A is at -4.5 and point B is at 2.75. What is the distance between points A and B? Enter the number only.

tr.1.75: Computed 4.5 - 2.75 (or -4.5 + 2.75) and ignored that the points are on opposite sides of 0.
tr.-7.25: Subtracted in the order A - B; distance is the absolute value of the difference.

w: Distance = |B - A| = |2.75 - (-4.5)| = |2.75 + 4.5| = 7.25. The points are on opposite sides of 0, so the distance is 4.5 + 2.75.

q: A quality report lists four measurement errors: -9.2, 9.15, 8.7 and -8.95. Which error has the greatest absolute value?
w: Absolute value is distance from 0: |-9.2| = 9.2, |9.15| = 9.15, |8.7| = 8.7, |-8.95| = 8.95. The greatest is 9.2, from -9.2.

n.0: 9.15 is the greatest number, but its distance from 0 (9.15) is less than 9.2.
n.2: |-8.95| = 8.95, which is less than 9.2.
n.3: |8.7| = 8.7, the smallest absolute value of the four.

q: On a number line, point Q is located exactly halfway between -1/2 and 3/4. What is the value of point Q?
w: The midpoint is the average: (-1/2 + 3/4) ÷ 2 = (-2/4 + 3/4) ÷ 2 = 1/4 ÷ 2 = 1/8. Check: from -1/2 up 5/8 gives 1/8, and from 1/8 up 5/8 gives 3/4.

n.0: 1/4 is the sum -1/2 + 3/4; it still needs to be divided by 2.
n.2: 5/8 is half of the distance between the points (1 1/4 ÷ 2), not the location of the midpoint.
n.3: -1/8 has the wrong sign; -2/4 + 3/4 is positive.

q: A medication refrigerator is set to 40°F. Its temperature t is acceptable when |t - 40| ≤ 3. Which recorded temperature is NOT acceptable?
w: |36.5 - 40| = |-3.5| = 3.5, which is greater than 3, so 36.5°F is not acceptable.

n.0: |43 - 40| = 3, and 3 ≤ 3 is true, so 43°F is acceptable.
n.2: |42.5 - 40| = 2.5, which is within 3 degrees.
n.3: |37 - 40| = 3, and 3 ≤ 3 is true, so 37°F is acceptable (the boundary is included).

q: Four points are plotted on a number line at -0.35, 0.4, -1/3 and 3/8. Which point is closest to 0?
w: Compare distances from 0 (absolute values): 0.35, 0.4, 0.375 and 1/3 ≈ 0.333. The smallest distance is 0.333..., so -1/3 is closest to 0.

n.0: |0.4| = 0.4, the farthest from 0 of the four.
n.1: 3/8 = 0.375, which is farther from 0 than 0.333...
n.3: |-0.35| = 0.35, which is greater than 1/3 ≈ 0.333.

q: On a number line, point R is at -1.2, point S is at -1 1/4, point T is at -1.23 and point U is at -1 1/8. Which point is farthest to the left?
w: Farthest left means least. As decimals: R = -1.2, S = -1.25, T = -1.23, U = -1.125. The least is -1.25, so point S is farthest left.

n.0: -1.2 is greater than -1.23 and -1.25, so R is to the right of both.
n.1: -1 1/8 = -1.125 is the greatest of the four, so U is farthest right.
n.3: -1.23 is greater than -1.25 (closer to 0), so T is to the right of S.

q: A number line has tick marks labeled -3 and 5, with 3 unlabeled tick marks evenly spaced between them. What value does the second unlabeled tick mark to the right of -3 represent?
w: 3 tick marks between the labels create 4 equal intervals. The distance from -3 to 5 is 8, so each interval is 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Second tick: -3 + 2 × 2 = 1.

n.0: -1/3 divides 8 into 3 intervals and stops at the first tick.
n.1: 2 1/3 divides 8 into 3 intervals; 3 tick marks between the labels make 4 intervals.
n.3: -1 is the first unlabeled tick (-3 + 2), not the second.

q: On Monday a checking account was at -45 dollars, and on Tuesday it was at 30 dollars. Which expression gives the distance between -45 and 30 on a number line?
w: Distance between a and b is |b - a|: |30 - (-45)| = |30 + 45| = 75.

n.0: |30| - |-45| = 30 - 45 = -15; a difference of absolute values is not the distance.
n.2: 30 - 45 = -15 drops the negative sign of -45 and gives a negative distance.
n.3: |30 + (-45)| = 15 adds the numbers instead of subtracting them.

q: Five values are to be plotted on a number line: |-2.5|, -|3|, -2 1/4, 1.9 and |-1/2|. Place them in order from left to right on the number line, starting with the leftmost.
w: Evaluate each first: -|3| = -3, -2 1/4 = -2.25, |-1/2| = 0.5, 1.9, |-2.5| = 2.5. Left to right is least to greatest: -3 < -2.25 < 0.5 < 1.9 < 2.5. Note that |-2.5| is positive, while -|3| is negative because the negative sign is outside the bars.

q: A lab balance displays the mass of a sample as 47.0652 grams. The lab report requires masses rounded to the nearest hundredth of a gram. What mass should be reported?
w: The hundredths digit is 6. The digit to its right (thousandths) is 5, so round up: 47.0652 → 47.07 g.

n.0: 47.065 g rounds to the nearest thousandth.
n.2: 47.1 g rounds to the nearest tenth, not the nearest hundredth.
n.3: 47.06 g truncates; the next digit is 5, so the hundredths digit rounds up.

q: A nursing program needs lab coats for 150 students and 8 instructors. It already has 10 new coats in storage, and more coats come only in boxes of 12. What is the least number of boxes the program must order so that everyone gets a coat?
w: Coats needed: 150 + 8 = 158. Subtract the 10 in storage: 158 - 10 = 148. Boxes: 148 ÷ 12 = 12.33. Twelve boxes hold only 144 coats, so round up to 13 boxes (156 coats, enough for the 148 still needed).

n.0: 12 boxes rounds 12.33 down; 12 boxes plus storage give 144 + 10 = 154 coats, 4 short.
n.1: 11 boxes subtracts the 8 instructors instead of adding them (150 - 8 - 10 = 132, and 132 ÷ 12 = 11).
n.3: 14 boxes ignores the 10 coats in storage (158 ÷ 12 = 13.17, rounded up), so it orders one box too many.

q: A regional hospital system reported serving 248,513 patients last year. What is this number rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
w: The ten-thousands digit is 4 (in 248,513). The digit to its right is 8, which is 5 or more, so round up: 250,000.

n.0: 200,000 is rounded to the nearest hundred thousand.
n.1: 249,000 is rounded to the nearest thousand.
n.3: 240,000 truncates; the thousands digit 8 means rounding up.

q: A clinic buys 38 boxes of syringes at $19.75 per box. Rounding each number to the nearest ten, which is the estimate of the total cost?
w: 38 rounds to 40 and $19.75 rounds to $20. Estimate: 40 × $20 = $800. (The exact cost is $750.50.)

n.0: $400 rounds $19.75 down to $10; the ones digit 9 means rounding up to $20.
n.1: $300 truncates both numbers (30 × $10) instead of rounding.
n.2: $600 rounds 38 down to 30; the ones digit 8 means rounding up to 40.

q: A dosage calculation gives a volume of 3.96 mL, and the syringe being used is marked in tenths of a milliliter. What is 3.96 rounded to the nearest tenth? Enter the number of milliliters only.

w: The tenths digit is 9. The hundredths digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so the 9 rounds up to 10, carrying 1 into the ones place: 3.96 → 4.0 mL (entered as 4).

q: A prescriber orders 0.15 mg of a drug for each kilogram of body weight. The patient weighs 72.6 kg. What is the dose? Do not round until the final answer, and round it to the nearest tenth of a milligram. Enter the number only.

w: Dose = 0.15 × 72.6 = 10.89 mg. Round only at the end: the hundredths digit is 9, so 10.89 → 10.9 mg.

q: A multidose vial contains 20 mL of medication, and 4.5 mL has already been drawn from it. Each dose is 1.5 mL. How many more full doses can be drawn from the vial?
w: Medication left: 20 - 4.5 = 15.5 mL. Doses: 15.5 ÷ 1.5 = 10.33. Only complete doses count, so round down: 10 full doses (10 × 1.5 = 15 mL; 0.5 mL is left over).

n.1: 14 ignores the 4.5 mL already drawn and also rounds 13.33 up instead of down.
n.2: 11 rounds 10.33 up; 11 doses would need 16.5 mL, but only 15.5 mL is left.
n.3: 13 ignores the 4.5 mL already drawn (20 ÷ 1.5 = 13.33, rounded down).

q: A county health survey found that 48.7% of the 6,120 adults surveyed exercise at least three times a week. Which is the best estimate of the number of adults who exercise that often?
w: 48.7% is close to the benchmark 50% = 1/2, and 6,120 is close to 6,000. Estimate: 1/2 × 6,000 = 3,000. (Exact: about 2,980.)

n.0: 2,400 truncates 48.7% to 40% (0.4 × 6,000); 48.7% is much closer to 50%.
n.2: 3,500 rounds 6,120 up to 7,000 before halving; to the nearest thousand, 6,120 is 6,000.
n.3: 2,000 uses the benchmark 1/3, but 48.7% is much closer to 1/2.

q: To estimate 6.8 × 4.6, a student rounds both numbers to the nearest whole number and calculates 7 × 5 = 35. How does this estimate compare with the exact product?
o: An exact estimate, because the rounding errors are both less than 0.5
An underestimate, because 4.6 was rounded more than 6.8
An overestimate by 0.6, the total amount the factors were rounded up
An overestimate, because both factors were rounded up
w: Both factors were rounded up (6.8 → 7 and 4.6 → 5), so the estimate is too high. Exact: 6.8 × 4.6 = 31.28, so 35 is 3.72 too high.

n.0: The rounding errors are small, but they still change the product (35 vs 31.28).
n.1: Rounding both factors up makes the product larger, so the estimate is too high, not too low.
n.2: The round-offs are multiplied by the other factors, so the error is 35 - 31.28 = 3.72, not 0.6.

q: A hospital department logged 2,749.5 overtime hours last year. What is 2,749.5 rounded to the nearest hundred?
w: The hundreds digit is 7. Look only at the digit to its right (tens), which is 4, so keep 7: 2,700.

n.2: 2,750 rounds to the nearest ten, not the nearest hundred.
n.3: 3,000 rounds to the nearest thousand.

q: A travel nurse worked 38.5, 41.2, 39.8, 40.6 and 39.1 hours over five weeks. Which is the best estimate of the total number of hours she worked?
w: All five values cluster near 40, so estimate 5 × 40 = 200 hours. (Exact: 199.2 hours.)

n.2: 220 rounds every value up to the next ten (40 + 50 + 40 + 50 + 40) instead of to the nearest ten.
n.3: 170 truncates each value to the tens place (30 + 40 + 30 + 40 + 30) instead of rounding.

q: Three coworkers split a $47.83 lunch bill equally. Each person's share is rounded up to the next cent so that the bill is fully covered. How much does each person pay?
w: $47.83 ÷ 3 = $15.9433... Rounding up to the next cent gives $15.95. Check: 3 × $15.95 = $47.85, which covers the bill.

n.0: $16.00 rounds up to the next dollar, not the next cent.
n.2: $15.90 rounds down to the nearest ten cents and leaves the bill short.
n.3: $15.94 is ordinary rounding; 3 × $15.94 = $47.82, which is 1 cent short.

q: A nurse started her shift at 6:45 a.m. and clocked out at 7:20 p.m. the same day. How long was she at work?
w: From 6:45 a.m. to 6:45 p.m. is 12 hours. From 6:45 p.m. to 7:20 p.m. is 15 + 20 = 35 minutes. Total: 12 h 35 min.

n.0: 11 h 35 min borrows an hour twice; only one hour is borrowed to turn 20 minutes into 80.
n.1: 13 h 25 min subtracts the hours (19 - 6 = 13) and then the smaller minute value from the larger (45 - 20) instead of borrowing an hour.
n.3: 12 h 25 min subtracts 20 from 45 minutes; from :45 to :20 of the next hour is 35 minutes.

q: A patient is prescribed 1.5 tablets three times a day. The pharmacy dispenses 90 tablets. How many full days will the supply last?
w: Tablets per day: 1.5 × 3 = 4.5. Days: 90 ÷ 4.5 = 20 days.

n.1: 60 days divides 90 by 1.5 tablets and ignores the three doses each day.
n.2: 135 days multiplies 90 by 1.5 instead of dividing.
n.3: 30 days divides 90 by 3 doses and ignores the 1.5 tablets per dose.

q: Jordan earns $2,850 per month after taxes. Each month he pays $1,140 in rent, spends 1/6 of his after-tax income on food and puts $300 into savings. How much money does he have left each month?

q: A 24-ounce bag of brown rice costs $4.56. A 2.5-pound bag of the same rice costs $7.20. Which bag costs less per ounce, and by how much?
w: 24-oz bag: $4.56 ÷ 24 = $0.19 per ounce. 2.5-lb bag: 2.5 × 16 = 40 oz, and $7.20 ÷ 40 = $0.18 per ounce. The 2.5-lb bag is cheaper by $0.19 - $0.18 = $0.01 per ounce.

n.0: This reverses the comparison; $0.18 per ounce is less than $0.19 per ounce.
n.2: $2.64 compares the bag prices, not the price per ounce.
n.3: $0.10 per ounce uses 1 lb = 10 oz (25 oz in the bag); 1 lb = 16 oz.

q: A home health nurse drives 24 miles at an average of 32 miles per hour to reach her first patient, then 35 miles at 60 miles per hour to reach her second. What is her total driving time?
w: Time = distance ÷ speed. Leg 1: 24 ÷ 32 = 0.75 h = 45 min. Leg 2: 35 ÷ 60 = 7/12 h = 35 min. Total: 45 + 35 = 80 min = 1 h 20 min.

n.0: 1 h 33 min reads 1.33 hours as 1 hour 33 minutes; 0.33 h is about 20 minutes.
n.1: 1 h 17 min divides the total distance by the average of the two speeds (59 ÷ 46); the legs must be timed separately.
n.3: 45 min is the time for the first leg only.

q: A hospital pharmacy receives 1,200 vials of a vaccine. It sends 3/8 of the vials to the intensive care unit, and then sends 2/5 of the remaining vials to the emergency department. How many vials are left in the pharmacy?
w: ICU: 3/8 × 1,200 = 450, leaving 750. Emergency department: 2/5 × 750 = 300. Left: 750 - 300 = 450 vials.

n.0: 300 is the number sent to the emergency department, not the number left.
n.2: 750 is the number left after the first step, before the emergency department's share.
n.3: 270 takes 2/5 of the original 1,200 (480) instead of 2/5 of the remaining 750.

q: A medication is given every 6 hours. The first dose was given at 2140 (24-hour clock). At what time is the third dose due, in 12-hour time?
w: Second dose: 2140 + 6 h = 0340. Third dose: 0340 + 6 h = 0940, which is 9:40 a.m. The third dose comes two intervals (12 hours) after the first.

n.0: 3:40 a.m. (0340) is the second dose.
n.2: 3:40 p.m. adds three 6-hour intervals (18 h); the third dose is only two intervals after the first.
n.3: 0940 is before noon, so it is 9:40 a.m.; 9:40 p.m. would be written 2140.

q: A community clinic saw 1,248 patients in the first quarter of the year and 1,575 in the second quarter. Its goal for the first half of the year was 3,000 patients. How many more patients would the clinic have needed to meet its goal?
w: Patients seen: 1,248 + 1,575 = 2,823. Shortfall: 3,000 - 2,823 = 177 patients.

n.0: 327 is how many more patients were seen in the second quarter than in the first.
n.1: 2,823 is the number of patients seen, not the number still needed.
n.2: 1,425 subtracts only the second quarter's patients from the goal.

q: A patient must take 2 tablets three times a day for 14 days and already has 25 of these tablets at home. More tablets are sold only in bottles of 30. How many bottles must be purchased to complete the full course?
w: Tablets needed: 2 × 3 × 14 = 84. Subtract the 25 at home: 84 - 25 = 59. Bottles: 59 ÷ 30 = 1.97. One bottle is not enough, so round up to 2 bottles (60 tablets, enough for the 59 still needed).

n.0: 1 bottle rounds 1.97 down; 30 + 25 = 55 tablets would run out before the 84 needed.
n.1: 3 bottles ignores the 25 tablets at home (84 ÷ 30 = 2.8, rounded up), so it buys one bottle too many.
n.2: 4 bottles adds the 25 tablets at home to the 84 needed (109 ÷ 30 = 3.63) instead of subtracting them.
